TLDR; I was told twice in a day that I must have a high metabolism because of my size.

Hello shitfamily. I am usually a very busy shitlady and rarely get any time off. Today I ended up having a halfday at one of my jobs and decided to go to a gym close by I had been meaning to check out and then get some groceries afterwards.

I went to the gym and went on a tour. It was perfect for what I was looking for so I decides to sign up. I got asked the normal questions of what my goals are, what are my exercise and eating habits now, etc. I explained I wanted to work on my body so I could become a personal trainer. I told them that I haven't been to a gym in a while and have been giving into some pizza cravings lately, but have been running 5 days a week and doing body weight exercises. The person chuckled and said, " you are lucky to have such a high metabolism."

I didn't expect to hear that so I ended up stumbling over my words a bit, "uh...I can't say it's that but I do like to think that maybe my uptake in cardio has helped me maintain my weight." He just laughed again.

After I got my gym membership, I walked to the grocery store and ended up getting more than my little arms could carry back home so I decided to call a cab. The cab driver picked me up and asked me what I was doing with my day. I told him abo it the halfday and the gym and he ended up asking, "why do you need to go to the gym? You're already so thin."

To which I quickly questioned, "how do you think I stay thin?"

The cab driver replied, "I just guessed you had a high metabolism. I think fat is good on a woman. Where I'm from, fat means wealth."

I was, again, taken aback by the reply I could only say, "I am not a fan, personally."

I wish when people looked at me they thought, "she must take good care of herself" instead of "she must have a high metabolism/good genetics".
TIL: people assume I am thin due to a high metabolism.

It's totally stupid but I think people need to say this to make themselves feel better. How else are they going to rationalize being out of shape when eating "normally" and I put that in quotes. If you talk to very lean guys (talking around or under 10% bf) about their diet, they say "I don't really like eating that much". Surpise, surprise.

It's like the "oh he's skinny because he's young" thing. Oh yea, there are fuckloads of fat 20-year-olds waddling about now, so how's that possible? I'm middle-aged and I'm not fat, so how did that happen? I find that young=thin/fit and old=fat myth just as annoying and as hard to dispel.

It's because when you're young you have more free-time and often higher test which does promote muscle growth. So you naturally live a more active lifestyle and (while still growing) use more calories. But if your habits are shitty then it's just a matter of time whether you'll be fat at 5, 15 or 25. If you have good habits you'll stay lean the entire time.

TLDR: Natural growth of body can make up for shitty habits while still young.
